body:
I think this doesn't work. Suppose we have:

```
      0x06, 0x00, 0xFF,  // Usage Page (Vendor Defined 0xFF00)
      0x09, 0x01,        // Usage (0x1)
      0x05, 0x01,        // Usage Page (Generic Desktop)
      0xa1, 0x01,        // Collection (Application)
```

The second Usage Page item should overwrite the global usage page value; the Collection usage should have the updated value (Generic Desktop 0x0001), not the original value (Vendor Defined 0xFF00).

body:
Oof, went down a bit of a rabbit hole here.

The spec is kinda contradictory:
- Under section 6.2.2.7, the Usage Page tag includes the sentence "Any usage that follows which is defines 16 bits or less is interpreted as a Usage ID and concatenated with the Usage Page to form a 32 bit Usage.", which to me agrees with this PR and disagrees with your interpretation.
- But the Remarks under section 6.2.2.8 include the sentence "When the parser encounters a main item it concatenates the last declared Usage Page with a Usage to form a complete usage value.", which disagrees with this PR and agrees with your interpretation.

Some more contradictory data points:
- Chromium (if I'm reading this right) seems to follow this PR - when it encounters a Usage tag it [applies the currently active Usage Page](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:services/device/hid/hid_item_state_table.cc;l=113-115;drc=568680270312cbbd2d9afccae94461ea7af8e05d).
- Linux started by [using your interpretation](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/58e75155009cc800005629955d3482f36a1e0eec) (while also noting the somewhat contradictory spec), and then that broke some Primax keyboards so [they moved to a heuristic that looks at whether the page has been used before](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/1cb0d2aee26335d0bccf29100c7bed00ebece851).

So in short, this is a mess! What do you think we should do here?
